Rye Brook Recreation is committed to providing quality recreation pro-

grams. In the winter months, our recreation programs are usually moved inside the schools, Bellefair gym and the Anthony J. Posillipo Community Center to get our participants out of the frigid temperatures. We will be having a few new programs this winter which include Pre K Mult-Sport and Hi-Five Little Ballers which are both run by Hi-Five Sports. In addition, we will be rolling out My First Hot Cocoa Stand, Chain Reaction Engineers and Snapology: Science of Superpowers for the first time this Winter. Please see the program descriptions within this brochure. In addition to these new initiatives, there are other staples in the book along with our ongoing Youth and Adult Basketball programs.
On-line registration for winter activities will begin on Friday, January 2nd

at 9:30pm. Your Community Pass account will allow us to get the recreation information to your household in an efficient and timely manner. To register for programs, simply go to the Village’s website at www.ryebrook.org, scroll down the home page and you will see Programs and Activities that will bring you to Community Pass to register for programs.
Coming this Spring, the recreation department will be running the Little

League. We will be partnering with an outside organization to run our Pre-K and Rookie League programs. We will announce additional information as it becomes available. The Little League Parade will take place on Saturday April 11th. All Little Leaguers, Rookie Leaguers and Pre K T-Ballers will march in our annual Little League Parade from Ridge Street School to Pine Ridge Park to officially commence the Spring Season.
We hope that Rye Brook Recreation is meeting your recreational needs. I

join my staff in wishing you and your families a healthy and rewarding 2026 New Year and look forward to seeing you at some of our many recreational activities.
Happy Holidays,
Robert Bertolacci
Parks and Recreation Superintendent

Our Hi-Five Basketball clinic offers boys and girls a chance to play a different sport every week.

Our Hi-Five Basketball clinic offers boys and girls a chance to learn the exciting game of basketball. Through engaging drills and individualized instruction children will learn to dribble, pass, shoot, and defend. Our program is not only designed to teach the skills of the game, but our experienced coaches will emphasize effort, teamwork and sportsmanship.
Games take place on Saturday and Sunday afternoons. Prac-
tices will take place during the week for grades 4-7.
Grades 2-3 will have a 15 minute practice preceding a 45
minute game. If interested email the rec department.

Let's learn about Rube Goldberg machines! Inthis hands-on pro-
gram, campers build a varietyof complex contraptions to com-
plete a simpletask—such as ringing a bell—while learning
thebasic physics concepts of work, gravity, force and momen-
tum.Using simple machines like levers, wedges, wheels, axles,
pulleys and inclined planes,campers learn to understand mechani-
calconcepts in a fun way, while using their imagination!

Children will begin to explore the world of robotics as they build simple models that teach the fundamentals of robotic design.
Whether learning about sensors while building drills and magic wands or discovering ways that gears and pulleys create movement while building helicopters and robotic dogs, your child is sure to have a great time!

This Spring Rye Brook Little League will begin its’21st
season as an accredited Little League program. We plan on getting your 2026 Little League season underway earlier so that we can have more structured practices prior to the start of the season. The Youth baseball and Little League softball ratings will take place in early March.
Coaches will attend a mandatory coaches clinic to enhance their ability to teach the skills to our Little Leaguers. There will be practices built into the first half of the season on a weekly basis.
Rye Brook Little League will have a dedicated website. The website will be the location to go to find out your league standings, scores, rosters, cancellations and statistics.
The minor league baseball program will utilize a pitching machine for all league games. There will be clinics every Friday afternoon emphasizing pitching, hitting and fielding.

The 2026 Rye Brook Little League will have playoffs for all Major league teams culminating in a Rye Brook Champion. We hope to see everyone at the ratings and hope to provide you with a wonderful and memorable Little League season.

Rye Brook Day Camp will be offered to children entering Kindergarten (proof required) in September 2026 to 6th grade. The camp will be limited to 250 children. Residents are given preference until May 1, 2026 (first come first served).
All campers will attend camp at Crawford Park.
A limited number of scholarships are available for Rye Brook residents only. Those in need of camp scholarships should contact Rocco Furano by April 4, 2026 at rfurano@ryebrookny.gov The recreation department is looking to change the camp slightly in the coming year. We are hoping to announce the fees by mid January.

Day/Time:Mon-Fri (8:30am—4:00pm)

The Village of Rye Brook Recreation Department is part of the South East Consortium for Special Services Inc., which is a“not-for-profit”organization, dedicated to providing leisure services to eligible citizens with developmental or other disabilities. The South East Consortium offers a variety of programs and services in an effort to meet the physical, social, cultural and quality of life needs of children and adults of all ages and functioning abilities. We try to base all activities on the appropriateness of the participant and availability of resources. We welcome your participation. For further information, contact the South East Consortium, 740 West Boston Post Road, Suite 312, Mamaroneck, New York 10543 or call (914) 698-5232.

Rye Brook Travel Camp is for campers entering 7th, 8th, 9th, 10th graders (September 2026) .
Campers will go on 5 trips a week. All trips are included in the registration. The camp is limited to 40 campers who will be accepted on first come, first serve basis. If you have any questions/concerns please email Ben Becker at bbecker@ryebrookny.gov
The recreation department is looking to change the camp slightly in the coming year including possibly incorporating 6th graders. We are hoping to announce the fees by mid January.

Zumba is perfect for everybody and anybody! Each Zumba class is designed to bring people together to sweat it on.
How it Works: We take the“work”out of the workout, by

mixing low intensity and high intensity moves for an interval-style, calorie burning dance fitness party. Once the Latin and World rhythms take over, you’ll see why Zumba Fitness classes are often called exercise in disguise.
Benefits: A total workout, combining all elements for fit-
ness-cardio, muscle conditioning, balance and flexibility, boosting energy and a serious dose of awesome each time you leave class. No experience needed! 6 sessions.
